metaDescription: Six portable shower chairs compared on footprint, seat height, folding method and listed capacity, for tubs, small stalls and travel.
introParagraphs: A portable shower chair is judged by how it moves and how it stores, but it still has to behave like a stable seat the moment someone sits on it. That tension shapes every product here: folding frames, three-legged stools and aluminum or stainless tubes all trade carrying ease against how much bracing the seat gets. Wet floors and a person shifting their weight make the details of leg feet and locking points matter far more than they do on a dry stool.

We looked at six picks: a compact HOMLAND stool, a Brosive stainless folder, a UGarden folding seat with a C-buckle lock, the triangular FULLOT, a Medline backless bench with arms, and the small GOYUWEN folding seat. They were compared on listed footprint, seat height range, how the frame folds or assembles, drainage and the capacity each page states. Anything the listing leaves out is flagged rather than assumed.

None of this is a medical recommendation. Check the stated capacity against the person who will sit, measure the tub or stall floor, and ask a physical or occupational therapist when balance, transfers or recovery are involved.

products.name: FULLOT Space-Saving Triangular Shower Chair
products.description:
FULLOT builds this chair as a triangle with three adjustable tubes that slot into the seat, and the page claims the whole assembly takes around nine seconds. The footprint measures 17.8 by 15.7 in and the height spans 15.5 to 20.5 in, which is the tallest top setting in this group. A rear bracing design and a seat 4.5 mm thicker than the maker's usual are said to support the stated 400 lb rating.

Three legs take up less floor than four, and they pack down small, which is the point for a portable seat. The cost is that three points need a flat floor to sit steady, and a sloped or lipped tub bottom can make the seat rock. There is no back or arm, so the chair gives a place to sit and little else.

Against the UGarden at 17.5 in wide, the FULLOT has a similar width but a taller height ceiling. It stores more compactly than the Medline, whose arms enlarge the footprint. For a user who wants a seat that disappears into a cupboard, it is the cleanest option here.
products.bestFor: Small tubs and stalls where a seat must store out of the way.
pros: 17.8 by 15.7 in footprint is the smallest listed
Seat tops out at 20.5 in, the tallest here
Three tubes slot in with no tools needed
Seat is 4.5 mm thicker with rear bracing
cons: No back or arms, so support is minimal
Three legs need a flat floor to sit steady

products.name: Brosive Folding Shower Chair, Stainless Steel
products.description:
Brosive uses a heavy stainless steel frame with a triangular structure and lists support for up to 400 lb. The seat folds in two steps, measures 13.3 by 14.5 in between the legs, and carries built-in handles plus drainage holes that move water off the seat. The page positions it for home use and for travel, and for tubs that are narrower than usual.

Stainless is a different material choice from the aluminum used by most competitors. It resists rust, but it is also heavier to lift, so a person who plans to carry the chair between rooms or onto a trip should think about that. The handles help with carrying and with lifting the seat in and out of the tub.

Compared with the FULLOT, the Brosive folds rather than assembles, so setup is a hinge movement instead of slotting tubes. Its leg span is smaller than the UGarden's 17.5 in seat, which suits narrow tubs but gives less room under the sitter. As with every seat here, there is no backrest or armrest.
products.bestFor: Narrow tubs where a folding frame with built-in handles helps with carrying.
pros: Stainless frame listed to 400 lb
Leg span of 13.3 x 14.5 in suits narrow tubs
Built-in handles help carrying and lifting
Drainage holes move water off the seat
cons: No backrest or armrests for support
Stainless steel is heavier to carry

products.name: UGarden 17.5 in Folding Shower Chair with Pad
products.description:
UGarden pairs a folding stainless steel frame with a 17.5 in padded seat and a C-buckle that locks the frame in the open position. The page lists 400 lb capacity, eight drainage holes and built-in handles for setting the chair down or lifting it. The pad is the notable difference from the bare seats of the FULLOT and Brosive.

The lock is the feature to pay attention to. A folding seat is only a stable seat when the frame is fully open and latched, so the buckle gives you a physical step to confirm each time. Padding is more comfortable on the thighs, but it should be rinsed and dried to avoid soap residue.

It is wider than the Brosive's 13.3 by 14.5 in leg span, so it takes more tub floor, and heavier than aluminum options like the HOMLAND. The seat has no backrest. If seated comfort is the priority and the tub is not narrow, this is the folding model to look at first.
products.bestFor: A comfortable padded seat that still folds flat for storage.
pros: C-buckle locks the frame in the open position
Stainless steel frame listed to 400 lb
Eight drainage holes clear shower water
Padded 17.5 in seat is comfortable to sit on
cons: No backrest for users who need one

products.name: HOMLAND Adjustable Height Shower Stool
products.description:
HOMLAND makes this stool from reinforced aluminum alloy and lists a 400 lb capacity. Its seat height adjusts in 1 in increments, starting at 14 in, which lets you fit the seat to a user's knee height closely. The frame is compact and aimed at narrow bathtubs and small stalls.

The fine steps are the main reason to choose it. Most folding seats here move in coarser jumps or fix the height, so a short user or a tall one can land the seat where the knees sit comfortably. The aluminum alloy resists rust in damp rooms and weighs less than stainless.

It is a plain stool, with no back or arms, and the page does not give an exact seat width. Compared with the Medline, which adjusts from 16 to 21 in, the HOMLAND starts lower at 14 in and suits shorter users. Next to the FULLOT, it is less flat to store but easier to dial to height.
products.bestFor: Shorter users or anyone who needs a close height fit in a narrow tub.
pros: 1 in height steps allow close fitting
400 lb listed capacity on aluminum alloy
Compact frame aimed at narrow tubs
Reinforced alloy resists rust in wet rooms
cons: Plain stool with no back or arms
Exact seat width not given in the listing

products.name: Medline Backless Shower Chair with Arms
products.description:
Medline adds padded armrests to a backless aluminum bench, with legs that raise the seat 1 in at a time from 16 to 21 in. The listing gives a 350 lb capacity and a seat depth of 13.5 in, and says it fits most standard bathtubs. Slip-resistant feet hold the legs in place on wet surfaces.

Arms change how a person gets up. They offer something to push from when standing, which many users value, and they give the hands a place to rest while seated. The tradeoff is footprint: the arms widen the chair, so a very small tub or stall may not accommodate it.

It lists a lower capacity than the 400 lb options such as the FULLOT and HOMLAND, so check the weight rating against the user. The height range reaches 21 in, higher than the HOMLAND's starting range. If you want a bench with support at the sides without moving to a full chair back, this is the one.
products.bestFor: Users who want arms to push from when standing in a standard tub.
pros: Padded armrests give a push-up point
Seat height steps 1 in from 16 to 21 in
Slip-resistant feet hold the legs in place
Lightweight aluminum frame is easy to move
cons: Arms enlarge the footprint in a small tub
350 lb listed capacity is lower than others here

products.name: GOYUWEN Foldable Bath Shower Safety Chair Seat
products.description:
GOYUWEN is the smallest seat in the lineup: a foldable grey bench 15.7 in high with a seat measuring 12.4 by 8.3 in. The listing describes it as a safety chair for older adults and asks buyers to check the size before ordering, which is sensible given the seat is narrow. It folds for placement and storage and is the one most suited to a suitcase.

A seat this size will not suit everyone. The listed surface is shallow, and the page does not state a weight capacity in the details we reviewed, so there is no figure to compare with the 350 and 400 lb ratings elsewhere. It is for light, short-duration sitting where space is the main constraint.

Next to the FULLOT, with a 17.8 by 15.7 in footprint, it gives up a lot of seat area to gain portability. The Brosive offers handles and listed capacity that this one lacks. Use it only after confirming the size fits the person, and consider a larger model for regular daily use.
products.bestFor: Occasional travel use where the seat must fold small and the user is petite.
pros: Seat folds for placement and compact storage
15.7 in height is low and easy to step into
Anti-slip design noted on the product page
Smallest packed size of the six here
cons: Seat of 12.4 by 8.3 in is narrow for many users
No capacity figure in the details reviewed

buyingCriteria.explanation: Capacity is the first number to read, and the stated limit should sit well above the weight of the person using it. The Brosive, UGarden, HOMLAND and FULLOT list 400 lb, while the Medline lists 350 lb. A frame that bends at a joint or a leg that spreads under load is a poor sign, so use the label on the chair, not just the web page. The GOYUWEN page does not state a figure in the details we reviewed, which is a reason to confirm it with the seller.

A portable chair has to sit flat on the floor of the tub or stall without its legs on the drain or the curve. The FULLOT footprint measures 17.8 by 15.7 in and the Brosive leg span is 13.3 by 14.5 in. Measure the narrowest part of your floor before ordering, and leave a little room for the feet. Armrests such as the Medline's add width, so a narrow tub favors an armless seat.

A seat that is too low makes standing hard, and one that is too high leaves the feet dangling. The HOMLAND starts at 14 in and moves in 1 in steps, while the Medline reaches from 16 to 21 in and the FULLOT from 15.5 to 20.5 in. A common rule of thumb is a seat close to the height of the back of the knee while wearing nothing on the feet. A therapist can fine tune this.

A folding frame stores flat but adds a lock to check each time, while a fixed or slot-in frame is steadier but bulkier. The UGarden has a C-buckle that locks the frame open, and the Brosive folds in two steps. The FULLOT slots three tubes into the seat with no tools. Whatever you pick, confirm the frame is fully open and latched before sitting.

Rubber feet, drainage holes and a rust-resistant frame decide how a chair behaves in wet rooms. The UGarden lists eight drainage holes, the Brosive and UGarden use stainless steel, and the HOMLAND and Medline use aluminum alloy. Stainless is heavier to carry, and aluminum is lighter but relies on its coating. Wipe feet and frame after bathing and inspect them monthly.

Most portable seats are backless and armless to save space and weight, which is fine for stable users and not for everyone. The Medline is the only one with armrests, and none of the six has a backrest. If a user needs help to stand or to stay upright, a chair with arms and a back or a different type of seat may fit better, and an occupational therapist is the right person to ask.

howWeEvaluated.title: Footprint and fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the listed dimensions that decide whether a chair fits a narrow tub or small stall. The FULLOT at 17.8 by 15.7 in and the Brosive at 13.3 by 14.5 in lead for small spaces, while the Medline's arms add width. Dimensions come from each product page and were not measured by us.

howWeEvaluated.title: Stated capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: Listed capacity was compared across the six picks. The Brosive, UGarden, HOMLAND and FULLOT each list 400 lb, the Medline lists 350 lb, and the GOYUWEN does not state a figure in the details reviewed. The label on the chair itself should be the final word.

howWeEvaluated.title: Height adjustment
howWeEvaluated.description: Adjustment range and step size were scored. The HOMLAND offers 1 in steps from 14 in, the Medline spans 16 to 21 in, and the FULLOT reaches 20.5 in. The Brosive, UGarden and GOYUWEN pages give less height detail, which counts against easy fitting.

howWeEvaluated.title: Folding and setup
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at how each chair folds, locks or assembles. The UGarden's C-buckle gives a clear lock step, the Brosive folds in two steps, and the FULLOT slots in three tubes. Chairs with fewer moving parts scored better for ease and for fewer things to check.

howWeEvaluated.title: Wet room design
howWeEvaluated.description: Drainage, feet and material were compared. Eight drainage holes on the UGarden, rust-resistant stainless on the Brosive and aluminum alloy on the HOMLAND stood out. Padding and handles were noted as comfort and carrying aids, and value was judged on features offered per pick.

cards.label: Folding
cards.text: A hinged frame collapses flat and fits a closet or suitcase, but it must be fully open and latched. The Brosive, UGarden and GOYUWEN all fold. Choose this if storage is the problem and you will check the latch each time.

cards.label: Slot-in or rigid
cards.text: The FULLOT slots three tubes into the seat, and the HOMLAND and Medline use adjustable legs on a rigid bench. There is no hinge to forget, but the parts take more space to store. Pick this if the chair stays in the bathroom.

faq.q: Which portable shower chair is the smallest?
faq.a: The GOYUWEN is the smallest at 15.7 in high with a 12.4 by 8.3 in seat. For something sturdier that is still compact, the FULLOT measures 17.8 by 15.7 in and lists 400 lb. The Brosive has a 13.3 by 14.5 in leg span if the problem is a narrow tub.

faq.q: How do I know a folding chair is locked?
faq.a: The frame should be fully open, with any latch or buckle engaged and the legs level before you sit. The UGarden's C-buckle makes that step easy to confirm. If a lock feels loose, do not use the chair until it is fixed.

For many users it is, but a backless stool offers no support if you lean or lose balance. The Medline adds arms, and none of these six has a back. If you need to stay upright without help, ask a clinician or occupational therapist about a different seat.

faq.q: Does a higher capacity mean it is safer?
faq.a: Not by itself. Capacity is the maker's stated limit and does not describe how the chair feels when you sit or stand. Level feet, a locked frame and a seat height that suits the user matter at least as much.

faq.q: How do I clean and care for these chairs?
faq.a: Rinse off soap and shampoo after bathing and dry the feet and frame. Look for rust, loose bolts and worn rubber feet each month. The padded UGarden seat needs extra rinsing to avoid residue.

faq.q: Can I use one of these in a walk-in shower?
faq.a: Usually yes, if the floor is flat and the drain is not under the legs. Bathrooms with a slope toward the drain can make a three-legged seat like the FULLOT rock. Test with the legs on the actual floor before sitting for a full shower.

faq.q: Are these made for medical use?
faq.a: They are consumer bath seats, and the pages describe them for older and mobility-limited users. They are not a prescription or a treatment. A professional can help choose the right equipment for your needs.
